provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The constructor puts two same-coloured bars on the two opposite edge lines (original rows 0 and H-1). It puts a full divider line of colour 2 at the middle index. The 4s fill the cells strictly between the longer bar and the divider, but only at the positions where both bars are present. Under D4, a horizontal flip keeps the bars on rows. An odd number of clockwise turns moves them to the leftmost and rightmost columns, and the divider becomes a vertical column. The factory therefore picks the axis from d4%4 parity and emits a program that works directly in visible coordinates, with explicit row and column branches. Colour roles are fixed constants: background = palette[0], divider = palette[2], fill = palette[4]. Any other non-background cell on an edge line counts as bar. The program scans interior lines for one made entirely of the divider colour, falling back to the middle index if none is found. It takes the overlap of the occupied positions on the two edge lines and compares bar lengths. It then fills the half on the longer bar's side, excluding the edge line and the divider. Which edge is 'top' does not matter, because the rule is symmetric: it always fills the longer bar's half. So reflections and rotations need no extra direction handling beyond the axis choice.
draft_notes.limitations: Equal bar lengths never occur: the constructor rejects them. In that case the emitted program picks the first visible edge (row 0 or column 0), which matches the archived solver's choice of the top half only in unrotated orientations. Because this tie case is outside the generator's domain, it is not a real rule. Not tested by me. The generator also always produces a non-empty overlap and places the divider exactly at the middle index. The program does not depend on the divider being at the middle, except as a fallback when no full divider line is found. If the bar colour were ever palette[0], the bars would be invisible, but the generator excludes this through random_color. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found: all four train pairs and the test pair agree with the rule.
